source: National Archives Bill of Rights transcript, Amendment I
review_notes: Codex reviewed the complete frozen First Amendment sentence. Six clauses constrain laws Congress may enact; the text also expressly names the people’s rights to assemble peaceably and petition for redress. The reference to “thereof” resolves to religion. These are Codex labels, not independent human labels.
text:
Amendment I

Congress shall make no law respecting an establishment of religion, or prohibiting the free exercise thereof; or abridging the freedom of speech, or of the press; or the right of the people peaceably to assemble, and to petition the Government for a redress of grievances.
